title: Zearalenone and its metabolites provoke contrasting modulatory responses on estrogen and androgen receptors: Insights into the molecular basis of endocrine disruption in live cells.
authors: Rizvi, Sheeba; Chhabra, Ayushi; Sagurthi, Someswar R; Tyagi, Rakesh K
journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子对接和活细胞成像研究玉米赤霉烯酮及其代谢物与雌激素/雄激素受体的互作，虽涉及蛋白-配体对接，但对象为核受体而非TF-DNA，且无AI或MD方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEA) is a non-steroidal mycotoxin enrouted mainly through the consumption of contaminated dietary products. Some traditional studies with ZEA have implied influence on several cellular and endocrine processes. However, detailed advanced insights into the molecular basis of ZEA-induced toxicity under defined live-cell conditions remain unexplored. This study uses molecular docking and cell-based approaches to investigate the interactions between ZEA, its metabolites (⍺-ZOL, beta-ZOL), steroid receptors ERalpha/beta, and androgen receptor (AR). The studies were performed with HEK293T and HepG2-derived stable cell lines exposed to 1 muM of ZEA, ⍺-ZOL, beta-ZOL, and cognate steroids, 17beta-estradiol, and 5⍺-DHT (10 nM). Fluorescent protein-tagged cytoplasmic-shifted ER⍺/beta and AR chimeras enabled visualization of receptor-xenobiotic interactions under live-cell conditions. Key parameters examined included i) receptor subcellular localization, ii) ligand-receptor interactions, iii) transcriptional function, and iv) receptor-chromatin interactions. Competitive reporter-gene assays were also performed with ⍺-ZOL and beta-ZOL (0.1-1.0 muM) in the presence of 5⍺-DHT (EC50; 10(-10) M). ZEA metabolites promoted i) ER⍺/beta and AR nuclear translocation, ii) ERalpha/beta transactivation, iii) repression of DHT-induced AR transactivation, and iv) contrasting receptor-chromatin interactions. This study suggests that endocrine disruptions are driven by a complex interplay of agonistic and/or antagonistic effects of ZEA and its metabolites on receptor function, contributing to potential health risks.
abstract_zh: 玉米赤霉烯酮（ZEA）是一种非甾体类真菌毒素，主要通过摄入受污染的膳食产品进入体内。一些传统研究表明，ZEA对多种细胞和内分泌过程有影响。然而，在明确的活细胞条件下，ZEA诱导毒性的分子基础尚未得到深入的先进见解。本研究采用分子对接和基于细胞的方法，探讨ZEA、其代谢物（⍺-ZOL、β-ZOL）、类固醇受体ERα/β以及雄激素受体（AR）之间的相互作用。实验使用HEK293T和HepG2来源的稳定细胞系，暴露于1 μM的ZEA、⍺-ZOL、β-ZOL及相应类固醇（17β-雌二醇和5⍺-DHT，10 nM）。荧光蛋白标记的细胞质移位ER⍺/β和AR嵌合体使得在活细胞条件下可视化受体-外源物相互作用成为可能。检查的关键参数包括：i) 受体亚细胞定位，ii) 配体-受体相互作用，iii) 转录功能，以及iv) 受体-染色质相互作用。此外，在5⍺-DHT（EC50；10(-10) M）存在下，对⍺-ZOL和β-ZOL（0.1-1.0 μM）进行了竞争性报告基因实验。ZEA代谢物促进了i) ER⍺/β和AR核转位，ii) ERα/β反式激活，iii) 抑制DHT诱导的AR反式激活，以及iv) 对比性受体-染色质相互作用。本研究提示，内分泌干扰是由ZEA及其代谢物对受体功能的激动和/或拮抗效应的复杂相互作用驱动的，从而构成潜在的健康风险。
